Tools.name: input_record
Tools.description: Starts a tick-zero recording or saves its validated applied inputs, expectations and state-hash checkpoints (one every 60 ticks). Stop checks output write permission. Every recording is first replayed with its input events, if any (the verification, which replaces the play session as input.replay does): unless that run reproduces every checkpoint, the final hash and every expectation and raises no script error, Stop refuses to write it (Validation naming the first divergence, the run's outcome in error data verification), which catches a script.eval that wrote script state during the recording. Once the run passed, its scripts are stopped, and an error their OnDestroy raises refuses the recording too (named at teardown). A recording without input events is then written, and the play session is the verification's, paused at its final tick with its scripts stopped (script.eval in the play context is refused there; scene.query and entity.get read its final state). One with input events is then replayed without them (the input check); when that run also reproduces every checkpoint, the final hash and every expectation, whatever script errors it raises, the recording's outcome does not depend on its input and Stop refuses to write it (Validation, the check's outcome in error data inputCheck). The play session is then the last run's, paused where it ended. End such a recording while the played state is still in the scene.

Tools.name: input_replay
Tools.description: Replays recorded inputs in a fresh session; verification failures retain every expectation and hash outcome in error data. strictHash compares the state hash at each checkpoint and at the final tick and, unless continuePastCheckpoint, stops at the first checkpoint that differs. The state hash covers the simulated world (entities and their serialized components, the tick, Random, id draws, physics), never script tables, so expectations observe script state. withoutInput replays without the input events, the check that the replay depends on its input. Afterwards the session stays paused at the replay's last tick (or where playback stopped), so script.eval, scene.query and entity.get read its final state; play.stop ends it.

The replay still fails when any checkpoint differed (checkpointsFailed, firstFailedCheckpointTick). With withoutInput it tells a replay whose final hash alone does not depend on its input.

Tools.name: script_errors
Tools.description: Reads the game's retained script errors without clearing them, including updated repeat counts, never a failed script.eval's: in the editor the current play session's (a new play session forgets the earlier sessions' errors and keeps the cursor), in the Runtime its process's. An error's tick is the tick its callback ran in, as Time.GetTick() reads it there (0 in the first fixed step; in the frame phase the ticks completed). Whatever pauseOnError says, the faulting behaviour instance is disabled at its first error and runs no further callback (its tasks cancelled) until a hot reload of its script, so its error's count does not grow; other instances and the entity's other slots run on, and pauseOnError only decides whether the editor also pauses play.

Tools.name: script_write
Tools.description: Writes source as one undoable edit and returns full compile/type diagnostics; invalid source remains saved. The result also gives the written source's line count and content hash (as script.read reports them) and changedLines, a single span from the first to the last changed line against the replaced source (its old and new line ranges, not a diff; null for unchanged bytes), so an edit can be checked to change only the lines it meant to. A dry run reports the same.

Tools.name: test_run
Tools.description: Runs configured tests and returns every outcome (counts, failedCases and the case rows; a replay's suite entry counts the checkpoints it compared) plus JSON/JUnit reports. The coverage object always keeps its registryFingerprint and gates; its counters are returned only with coverage: true or Testing.CoverageGates. Optional recording is published only after strict replay verification and, with input events, the input check (§13.6: refused when a run without them still passes that verification, whatever script errors it raises), and reported in the recording block (format version, ticks, events, checkpoints, final hash, where the input check diverged, and for a replay written over an existing file whether its checkpoints, one every 60 ticks, and its final hash equal the replaced file's, which a change seen only between checkpoints leaves equal); a refused recording names the selected rows that did not pass. Runs play saved scene files, so test.run refuses (InvalidState, nothing run) while an open scene has unsaved changes and a selected suite or replay plays it: scene.save first.

inputSchema.title: TestRunParams
inputSchema.description: Run selected suites, cases and replays without altering authored scene state.

filter.description: Case-insensitive substring of suite/case or replay path; a filtered run resolves and validates only the suites and replays it selects.

timeoutTicks.description: Optional positive run-wide tick cap; omitted means no additional limit.

record.description: Optional project Assets .replay output; requires one selected suite and strict reproduction in ordinary play (every state-hash checkpoint, one every 60 ticks, and the final hash). A recording with input events is also replayed without them and refused when that run reproduces every checkpoint and the final hash too, whatever script errors it raises: its outcome does not depend on its input. The result's recording block describes the replay written and, when it replaces an existing file, whether its checkpoints and final state hash equal that file's.

coverage.description: Return coverage.counters in the result; without it they are left out unless the project sets Testing.CoverageGates. The JSON report at jsonPath always holds them.

expect.description: With record only: expectations ({tick, luau}, as input.record's stop takes them) written into the recorded replay; each must hold when the recording is verified with its input, before anything is written.

items.description: An authored replay assertion at a completed-tick boundary.

luau.description: Luau expression or chunk returning a truthy JSON value. A value that is not JSON fails the expectation with its Script error, a vector, Color or Quat included: only script.eval returns those as arrays.

ifRevision.description: Optimistic concurrency: fail with Conflict unless the revision (_meta.revision) of the scene the request addresses (in the editor, the open scene its scene target names, else the active one) still equals this value.

Tools.name: tilemap_paint
Tools.description: Writes cells of a Tilemap asset (0 erases a cell, k paints the palette's entry k - 1) and saves it, as one undoable command; the cells' chunks are created and removed as needed. The editor's tile brush paints through it. A running lockstep, recording, replay or test session sees the change only after it ends.

tilemap.description: The Tilemap asset: its id, its "Assets/..." path or another asset reference.

cells.description: The cells to write, 1 to 65536 of them, in order: a later entry for the same cell wins.

x.description: The cell's column: x grows to the right, cell 0's left edge at the tilemap entity's origin.

y.description: The cell's row: y grows upwards, cell 0's bottom edge at the tilemap entity's origin.

tile.description: The new cell value: 0 erases the cell, k paints the tilemap's palette entry k - 1.

Tools.name: ui_tree
Tools.description: Shows the scene's UI laid out in scene pixels: every active canvas and element (with includeInactive the inactive ones too, laid out as if active and marked inactive) with its rectangle, its canvas's scale, clip, visibility, components, text and widget, the box each text is laid out in and whether it overflows its rectangle, and in the play scene the session's focus, hover and press, as a compact text outline or a flat JSON list, optionally for one canvas and to a depth.

canvas.description: An entity with a UiCanvas whose UI alone is listed; omitted: every canvas.

depth.description: The most levels listed below each canvas; 0: unlimited.

format.description: Text: a compact outline (widgets as UiButton, UiToggle(on|off), UiSlider(<value>), UiScrollView(<x>,<y>) and UiTextInput("<text>"), an inactive canvas or element that includeInactive lists marked inactive, a text that reaches beyond its rectangle marked overflows, widgets marked disabled, focused, hovered or pressed); Json: a flat list of entries.

width.description: The scene resolution's width to lay out at, with height; omitted: the play session's own, or for the edit scene its game view's at the project's window size (a PixelPerfectCamera's reference resolution under one).

height.description: The scene resolution's height to lay out at, with width.

target.description: The scene to read; omitted: the play scene while playing, else the edit scene.

includeInactive.description: Also list the inactive canvases and elements (a hidden panel and its texts), each laid out, and its text measured, as if it were active, and marked inactive (active false); a copy of the scene as it is now is laid out at the scene resolution, the play scene's too, and the scene itself is only read. Tools.name: viewport_screenshot
Tools.description: Renders a view of the target scene afresh at width x height (the game view through the primary camera, the editor's scene view, or a camera entity), downscales it to maxDimension (by default the requested size, or 1024 without width and height) and writes it as a PNG whose path the result names. Needs a renderer (not --renderer none).

inputSchema.title: ViewportScreenshotParams
inputSchema.description: The params of viewport.screenshot: a fresh render of a view as a PNG.

view.description: The view to render: "Game" (the primary camera) or "Scene" (the editor's scene-view camera; not in the Runtime).

target.description: The scene to render; omitted: the play scene while playing, else the edit scene.

width.description: The rendered width in pixels, before maxDimension.

height.description: The rendered height in pixels, before maxDimension.

camera.description: A camera entity of the target scene (an EntityRef) to render through instead of the view's camera.

debugView.description: A debug view to render instead of the lit image: a RenderDebugView name, ignoring case ("Lit", the default, also for ""). A data view stores each value v as round(255 v), except LightCount's heat map: 0 lights black, 1 to 2 blue, 3 to 4 cyan, 5 to 8 green, 9 to 16 yellow, 17 to 32 orange (1, 0.5, 0), more red.

annotate.description: Capture-only annotations: labels=all, selection (selected), none or an EntityRef array; colliders, bounds, axes and navMesh (the scene's baked navigation mesh as polygon edges) are booleans. Unknown members and invalid references are rejected.

maxDimension.description: The larger side of the PNG at most this many pixels, the image downscaled to fit. Absent, it is the larger of width and height when either is given, so the PNG has the requested size, and 1024 otherwise.

inline.description: Also return the PNG as base64 in "data" when it is at most 30 KB; a larger one is only written (inlineOmitted).

keep.description: Write the PNG into Library/Automation/Kept/ (user://Automation/Kept/ without a writable project and in the Runtime), which no later editor session prunes, instead of Library/Automation/Out/.
